[uxr-debrief 2026-11-18]

30-minute session on where first-week users look for planning features, with Participant A (internal, owns first-run funnel metrics). Transcript source: the local recorder folder capture; the committed summary sits at interviews/new-user-navigation-study-timeline-discoverability-q4-2026-2026-11-18-summary.md.

What landed: New users try the header toolbar before the left navigation, and our funnel data puts about two thirds of first meaningful clicks in the top bar. The left rail reads as settings and admin rather than where work lives. Discovery inside the first session predicts planning in that same session; users who never find the timeline build nothing in week one. The guided tour gets clicked through rather than read, so a persistent navigation change looks stronger for the January decision.

Not covered: mobile breakpoints under 900 pixels, and the label wording for the timeline if it moves to the left navigation.

_Posted by Claude Code on behalf of Jordan Reyes._
